Senses.Explanation: To recognize is to identify the person, object, source, or point presented in an encounter. Masters make recognition answerable in public—raising a staff, pointing at a bench, or asking about a seamless stupa—rather than accepting a private claim.

Senses.Note: 7 independently reviewed witnesses delimit this sense.

Senses.Explanation: A vow text is a written declaration that records an undertaking and can be preserved and circulated as a document. Mizang Daokai’s preface recounts the concrete circumstance recorded in his vow text and the canon-printing undertaking that followed. The conduct record of Yongming Yanshou separately names a composition called the Six-Hundred Vow Text of Great-Vehicle Compassion and Wisdom; its grammar does not safely decide whether “six hundred” counts texts or belongs to one title. Catalogues and preface outlines treat the headword as a document type and title: the Yongjia collection has a tenth section for making vows, and another collection lists Yishan Ran’s vow text by name. The Five Lamps recurrence is retained as a recension, not counted as an independent new vow. Zen deployment keeps the promise public and durable by putting the undertaking into a preserved composition rather than leaving it as an unrecorded intention.
